_comment: Pilot allowlist: the first expansion beyond one company, ten real boards.
SEPARATE FROM config/sources-allowlist.json ON PURPOSE. That file is what a
production deployment collects from; this one is a local experiment against the
isolated test database. Merging them is a later, deliberate decision.
WHAT WAS CHECKED, on 2026-09-02, for every entry below:
* the board answers today -- upstream's sources/*.yml only records that someone
once found it, which is not the same thing
* robots.txt on the API host allows the path, fetched at probe time and again
before every collection run, and recorded in each run's manifest
* the posting count the board actually returned
WHAT WAS NOT CHECKED, and is not claimed: no company's terms of service were read,
and no permission was sought from anyone. robots.txt allowing a path is a machine-
readable hint about crawling, not a licence to the content behind it. These are
public ATS APIs that employers publish so their openings can be read programmatically,
which is why this is defensible for a small local pilot -- it is NOT a basis for
redistribution, for scale, or for anything user-facing without a proper review.
Counts below are what the board returned at probe time. They move.
NOT INCLUDED, and why -- recorded so the next round does not re-probe them blindly:
lever/kraken123  200 OK, robots allow, ZERO postings
lever/mistral    200 OK, robots allow, ZERO postings
lever/whoop      200 OK, robots allow, ZERO postings
lever/anyscale   200 OK, robots allow, 1 posting -- live, dropped only to keep the
pilot at ten; a candidate for the next round
A zero-posting board cannot be told apart from a company with no open roles by an
empty array alone, so none of these is marked dead -- only unused.
